topic_desc_basic: The Ashlands are the largest region of Vvardenfell, a dry, inhospitable wasteland of stone obelisks, ash mires, and sparse vegetation. Frequent ash storms spread the Blight. House Redoran controls the western edge, the Urshilaku Ashlanders roam the northwest, and the interior is largely empty except for Ghostgate and scattered ruins.

title: The Grazelands
topic_desc: The Grazelands, known as Sunna Guradan, are the pastoral plains of northeastern Vvardenfell, stretching from Falensarano north to the coast above Tel Vos and east to Zafirbel Bay, bounded by the Ashlands mountains to the west. Wickwheat and stoneflower dominate the flora, with hackle-lo shrubs flourishing in the south. Wild guar, alit, and shalk roam the grasslands, and Daedra including golden saints and ogrim wander the sparsely populated open. Most of the region falls under Temple authority. Nomadic Ashlanders form the primary population, anchored by the Ahemmusa and Zainab camps. House Telvanni maintains a growing presence through Tel Vos, Master Aryon's tower, and the settlement of Vos, positioning the House to make future claims. Significant ruins are few, limited to the Dwemer site of Nchuleft, the Daedric shrine Kushtashpi, and the strongholds Falensarano and Indoranyon.
topic_desc_basic: The Grazelands, or Sunna Guradan, are the pastoral plains of northeastern Vvardenfell, bounded by the Ashlands to the west and Zafirbel Bay to the east. Wickwheat and stoneflower dominate the landscape. Sparsely populated, the region falls under Temple authority and is primarily inhabited by nomadic Ashlanders of the Ahemmusa and Zainab camps. House Telvanni maintains a growing presence through Tel Vos and Vos.

title: Molag Amur
topic_desc: Molag Amur is a vast, arid volcanic region forming the southern expanse of Vvardenfell's Ashlands, distinguished from the north by its surface lava rivers and pools. Its dark rock and ash overlays support sparse flora like trama root and fire petal, while hosting kagouti, alit, and frequent Daedra including atronachs and scamps. Foyadas serve as primary routes toward pilgrim sites at Mount Assarnibibi and Mount Kand. No Great House dominates; inhabitants are largely renegade mages, though House Telvanni claims a foothold at Tel Uvirith and the Erabenimsun Ashlander tribe occupies the east. Tribunal mythology holds the region was home to monsters born of Molag Bal and Vivec.
topic_desc_basic: Molag Amur is a vast, harsh volcanic region in southern Vvardenfell, distinguished from the northern Ashlands by its surface lava flows. The arid, ash-covered land hosts sparse vegetation, hostile wildlife, and frequent Daedra. Foyadas provide travel routes to important Tribunal pilgrim sites. No Great House controls the region, though Ashlanders of the Erabenimsun tribe dwell in its eastern reaches.

title: Azura's Coast
topic_desc: Azura's Coast encompasses the numerous islands south and east of Vvardenfell, stretching from the southern isles east of Ald Sotha northward along the eastern coast and Zafirbel Bay, including three southeastern peninsulas where a shrine to Azura stands. The region is also called the Telvanni Coast, reflecting House Telvanni's firm hold over its desolate, rocky terrain. Tel Mora, Tel Aruhn, Sadrith Mora, Tel Fyr, and Tel Branora are its principal settlements. Wizards, sorcerers, necromancers, and Ashlander Mabrigashes occupy Velothi ruins and caves throughout, while ancient Telvanni lords—often millennia old—treat the Tribunal as peers rather than gods. Imperial and Temple authority barely extends beyond Sadrith Mora. Ancestral tombs and Daedric shrines dot the islands, and bandits plague travelers despite regular rainfall and hardy flora.
topic_desc_basic: Azura's Coast is the island-dotted region south and east of Vvardenfell, named for a shrine to the Daedric Prince on its southeastern peninsulas. House Telvanni claims most of this desolate coast, where wizard towers, ancestral tombs, and Daedric ruins stand among rocky shores and scattered Ashlander camps.

title: Sheogorad
topic_desc: Sheogorad is a wild maritime archipelago of approximately 28 islands in the Sea of Ghosts off Vvardenfell's northern coast. The region is defined by high pillar-like menhirs and treacherous submerged rocks that make marine navigation nearly impossible. Largely hostile and uninhabited, it experiences a colder climate than the Vvardenfell mainland. The sole accessible port, Dagon Fel, sits on the main island and can only be reached by skirting the region and approaching from the north.
topic_desc_basic: Sheogorad is a rugged archipelago of roughly 28 islands in the Sea of Ghosts off northern Vvardenfell. Treacherous rocks and menhirs make sailing here extremely dangerous. The cold, largely uninhabited region is accessible only through Dagon Fel, its sole port on the main island.

title: The West Gash
topic_desc: The West Gash forms the western highlands of Vvardenfell, a vast corridor of rocky scrubland stretching from Balmora and the Odai River north to the Sea of Ghosts at Khuul. Bounded by the Bitter Coast to the west and the Ashlands to the east, its terrain features natural rock bridges and arches inland, transitioning to sparse northern highland forest. House Redoran holds traditional jurisdiction, with councilors governing its northern, western, and southern districts, though House Hlaalu's control of Balmora and the Imperial-chartered Caldera—whose mining company holds an ebony monopoly—creates persistent factional tension. Imperial presence is anchored by Fort Moonmoth and Fort Darius. Blighted creatures occasionally threaten travelers, while ruined Daedric shrines attract Orcish worshippers.
topic_desc_basic: The West Gash comprises the western highlands of Vvardenfell, stretching from Balmora north to the Sea of Ghosts. This rocky scrubland, marked by natural rock bridges, separates the Bitter Coast from the Ashlands. Notable settlements include Balmora, Caldera, Gnisis, and Khuul, with Imperial garrisons and ebony mining operations alongside traditional Redoran governance.

title: The Clockwork City
topic_desc: The Clockwork City, also called the Brass-Throat, is the eponymous realm of Sotha Sil, crafted to replicate the mythic structures of Nirn in metallic miniature. Existing as a metaphysical plane within a seemingly mundane clockwork globe, its interior is an expansive mechanical world. It is regarded as an incomprehensibly powerful world-shaping device; altering the City may alter Tamriel itself. Accessible only via extraordinary magic—such as Barilzar's Mazed Band—the City is tended by Clockwork Apostles who seek to forge a perfected Second Nirn, free of Daedric influence. Its tunnels, filled with Dwemer-inspired machinery and Fabricants, represent the living god's ongoing endeavor to reshape the flawed Aedric creation.
topic_desc_basic: The Clockwork City is a legendary mechanical realm created by the god Sotha Sil. Hidden beneath Mournhold and accessible only by powerful teleportation magic, it is said to be a metallic simulacrum of Nirn. The Tribunal Temple guards knowledge of its existence, though its true purpose and inner workings remain a mystery to all but Sotha Sil's devoted followers.

title: Necrom
topic_desc: Necrom is one of the eight major mainland cities of Morrowind, perched on the Padomaic Ocean along the eastern edge of the Padomaic Crest. As the center of ancestor worship, it bears the moniker City of the Dead, yet it remains a teeming, bustling metropolis for commerce, pilgrims, and the mournful throughout day and night. While modern Dunmer have left many ancient customs behind, Necrom helps them reconnect with that lost part of their history and ancestry. The city is traditionally ruled by the Keepers of the Dead, a monastic order serving as caretakers of both the city and its vast necropolis. The Keepers answer to the authority of the Tribunal Temple, and the surrounding eastern coast falls under the domain of House Indoril. The city's cemeteries are known to harbor malevolent beings, requiring the faithful to bury their dead by daylight and depart before nightfall.
topic_desc_basic: Necrom is a major mainland city on Morrowind's eastern coast, renowned as the center of ancestor worship and called the City of the Dead. Despite its name, it bustles with commerce and pilgrims. The monastic Keepers of the Dead govern the city and its vast necropolis under the Tribunal Temple's authority, while House Indoril holds sway over the surrounding region.

title: Scribs
topic_desc: Scribs are the larval stage of the kwama, large insects native to Morrowind whose colonies form the basis of the Dunmer egg mining economy. Though not aggressive, scribs defend themselves by secreting a substance that induces paralysis. Scrib jelly is harvested as a common food and alchemical ingredient. The scrib's image appears on banners throughout Vvardenfell to denote nearby taverns, reflecting its deep cultural familiarity among the Dunmer.
topic_desc_basic: Scribs are the larval form of the kwama, large insects kept in colonies for their eggs. Though unaggressive, they can paralyze attackers. Scrib jelly is a common Dunmer food, and the scrib image marks tavern banners across Vvardenfell.

title: Silt Striders
topic_desc: Silt Striders are giant arthropods native to Morrowind, towering up to sixty feet high. Their tough carapaces allow them to endure Vvardenfell's harsh environments and survive the Ash Blight that exterminated many native species. Domesticated by the Dunmer, they serve as the primary civilian transport across an elaborate network connecting the island's cities. Caravaners steer the creatures by directly manipulating exposed organs and tissues using specialized hooks. Since the arthropods lack natural cavities, passenger and cargo compartments are hollowed directly into their chitinous shells. Cities like Gnisis and Molag Mar maintain dedicated docks to facilitate trade shipments. Desiccated remains frequently dot the Ashlands, testament to the creatures' enduring presence in the region.
topic_desc_basic: Silt Striders are towering giant arthropods native to Morrowind, commonly used as the primary means of civilian transport across Vvardenfell. Dunmer caravaners steer them by manipulating exposed organs with specialized hooks. Passengers and cargo ride in compartments hollowed directly into the creatures' chitinous shells.

title: Nix-Hounds
topic_desc: Nix-hounds are bloodsucking insectoid pack-hunters native to Morrowind, classified as arthropods related to kwama and nix-oxen. They use a proboscis to drain prey, leaving meat-husks for scavengers. Aggressive and fast, they ambush victims in the wild but can be tamed into loyal pets, trackers, and watch-hounds by skilled handlers. Their corrosive saliva demands caution, and they are vulnerable to ash mites and blight. Dunmer utilize nix-hound meat for food and chili, their eyes for trade, and their parts in tribal customs. House Hlaalu bred the Coldspring variant for foreign climates, while rogue nix-hounds present a larger, deadlier threat.
topic_desc_basic: Nix-hounds are bloodsucking insectoid pack-hunters native to Morrowind. Known for their speed and ambush tactics, they drain prey using a proboscis. Though dangerous in the wild, they can be tamed as loyal pets and trackers. Dunmer commonly use their sweet meat for food and their parts in various customs.

title: Kwama
topic_desc: Kwama are large insectoids native to Morrowind that live in underground communal colonies. Each colony centers on a single immobile queen, who produces all the nest's eggs, and is attended by workers who dig tunnels and maintain the brood. Foragers, aggressive worm-like scouts, search for new nesting sites and prey, while warriors protect the colony from invaders. The scrib is the larval form, capable of paralyzing threats. Dunmer operate egg mines to harvest kwama eggs as a dietary staple, making the creatures economically vital. Kwama are distant relatives of nix-hounds and susceptible to blight diseases, which increase their aggression.
topic_desc_basic: Kwama are large insectoids native to Morrowind that live in underground colonies. They have a rigid caste system: a queen produces eggs, workers dig tunnels, foragers scout, and warriors defend the nest. Scribs are their larval form. Dunmer heavily rely on egg mines to harvest kwama eggs for food.

title: Netch
topic_desc: Netch are large, generally peaceful creatures native to Morrowind that float through the air supported by internal sacks of magical gases, resembling airborne jellyfish. Males, called bull netches, are larger than the more easily provoked females, known as betty netches. Their tentacles bear barbs with active nematocysts, making them deadly when threatened. During breeding season, threatened betty netches and calves secrete pheromone oils that drive bull netches into aggression. Netch feed on fungi using a chitinous beak. They are hunted by Dunmer for their leather and other materials. Whether netch descended from the smaller Swamp Jellies of Black Marsh or originated independently remains debated among scholars.
topic_desc_basic: Large floating creatures native to Morrowind, netch resemble airborne jellyfish buoyed by internal gas sacks. Dunmer hunt them for their valuable leather. The larger males are called bull netches, while the smaller, more easily provoked females are known as betty netches. Though generally peaceful, their tentacle barbs can be deadly.

title: Guar
topic_desc: Guar are large bipedal omnivorous reptiles native to Morrowind and Black Marsh, serving as the primary domesticated herd animals of these provinces. Characterized by endurance and intelligence, they are essential as pack beasts and mounts for Velothi ranchers and Ashland nomads, and are raised for their hides, meat, and eggs. Though usually docile, wild guar can be territorial. They are kin to the alit and kagouti, and numerous breeds exist, from the common freckled guar to the rare albino white guar, which features prominently in Ashlander prophecies. Dunmer traditionally employ Saxhleel slaves as guar-herds, though whether the species originated in Black Marsh or Morrowind remains disputed.
topic_desc_basic: Guar are large bipedal reptiles native to Morrowind and Black Marsh. They are the primary domesticated herd animal of these regions, widely used as pack beasts and mounts. Dunmer raise them for hides, meat, and eggs. Usually docile, wild guar can become aggressive. Rare white guar hold significance in Ashlander prophecies.

title: Cliff Racers
topic_desc: Cliff racers are large, legless flying reptiles that dominate the skies of Morrowind. Recognizable by the prominent vertical sails along their spines and their lengthy tails, they include species such as the long-tailed and girdle-tailed varieties. Closely related to cliff striders and cliff darters, these creatures are notorious for their aggressive disposition and keen vision. They often detect travelers from great distances, descending in relentless swarms upon the unwary. Their pervasive presence makes them a constant hazard for hunters and Dunmeri travelers alike, earning them a widespread and bitter notoriety across the province.
topic_desc_basic: Cliff racers are large, aggressive flying reptiles ubiquitous across Morrowind. Distinguished by their legless bodies, long tails, and prominent vertical sails, they are a constant menace to travelers. With keen eyesight, they detect intruders from afar and attack in relentless swarms, making any journey through the province perilous.

title: Ash Vampires
topic_desc: Ash Vampires are powerful, high-ranking servants of Dagoth Ur, transformed through deep communion with his divine power and Corprus. Unlike lesser ash creatures, they retain considerable intelligence and arcane capability, serving as generals and lieutenants within House Dagoth. They are most commonly encountered within the Ghostfence and Red Mountain citadels, where they guard their master's strongholds and enact his will. Their distorted physiology reflects their profound connection to the Heart of Lorkhan.
topic_desc_basic: Ash Vampires are powerful, corrupted servants of Dagoth Ur. Transformed by his power and the Corprus disease, they serve as elite guardians and leaders within House Dagoth, primarily found in the Red Mountain region.

title: Werewolves
topic_desc: Werewolves are individuals afflicted with Sanies Lupinus, a contagious disease that transforms them into powerful, bloodthirsty beasts. During transformation, the subject's anatomy radically shifts: the heart swells first, followed by significant lengthening of the arms and feet, and the development of formidable claws. They exhibit severe bloodlust and stand notably taller than an Orc. Silver weapons are highly effective against them, while wolfsbane and belladonna prove toxic. The condition is widely feared across Tamriel, with active populations documented in regions like Skyrim and Morrowind, particularly on the island of Solstheim, where the Skaal have long contended with their presence.
topic_desc_basic: Werewolves are fearsome beasts afflicted with the contagious disease Sanies Lupinus. They stand taller than an Orc and possess immense strength, lethal claws, and a severe bloodlust. Silver weapons are notably effective against them, while wolfsbane and belladonna act as potent toxins. They are especially prevalent in Skyrim and on the island of Solstheim.

title: Magicka
topic_desc: Magicka is the raw arcane energy flowing from Aetherius into Mundus through the sun and stars, remnants of Magnus and the Magna Ge's departure from creation. Described as an aspect of the soul and the very sinews holding the planes together, it accumulates within mortals and is channeled to cast spells, enchant, and practice alchemy. A spellcaster's total magicka reserve is governed by their intelligence and racial or astrological affinities. Despite millennia of study by the Psijic Order and other scholars, fundamental mysteries regarding its generation and flow remain unresolved, and certain rare effects and artifacts can negate or silence its use entirely.
topic_desc_basic: Magicka is the raw energy used to cast spells and practice the arcane arts. It flows into Mundus from Aetherius through the sun and stars, and resides within all living souls. A spellcaster's available magicka is determined by their intelligence, and it naturally replenishes with rest.

title: Enchanting
topic_desc: Enchanting is the discipline of imbuing physical objects with magical properties, typically by trapping souls within soul gems to power the effect. Raven Direnni formalized the art in the First Era with her Rules of Eldritch Binding, dramatically reducing prior failure rates, though earlier grand enchanters like Ahzidal preceded her. The Ayleids extensively enchanted their possessions, and such durable artifacts remain highly prized. Vanus Galerion later standardized enchanting tools for public use, though he restricted their automation after laymen created dangerous objects. Today, the Mages Guild limits enchanting practice to higher-ranking members due to the temptation of Black Soul Gems. The craft overlaps with smithing, particularly in imbuing ebony with Daedric essences to forge Daedric gear. A skilled enchanter acts as a catalyst, drawing far greater power from an item than a novice could.
topic_desc_basic: Enchanting imbues objects with magical effects, usually by trapping souls in soul gems to power them. The Mages Guild restricts the practice to trusted members due to the dangerous temptation of Black Soul Gems. Skilled enchanters draw far greater power from an item than novices, and Ayleid enchanted artifacts remain highly prized possessions.

title: Alchemy
topic_desc: Alchemy is the art and science of identifying the magical properties inherent in ingredients and combining them to produce potions with diverse temporary or permanent effects, such as healing, curing disease, water-walking, magical shielding, and fortifying bodily attributes. A practitioner's skill determines the range of properties they can discern in a given substance, the likelihood of successfully brewing a potion, and the resulting magnitude and duration of its effects. The potency of crafted concoctions is further influenced by the quality of the apparatus employed—such as retorts, calcinators, alembics, and mortars—and the practitioner's intelligence and luck. It remains a potentially powerful discipline for those who master its intricacies.
topic_desc_basic: Alchemy is the practice of identifying the magical properties within ingredients and brewing them into potions. These concoctions can produce various effects, such as healing, curing disease, or fortifying attributes. A practitioner's skill determines how many properties they can discern in an ingredient and the potency of the resulting mixture.

title: Soul Gems
topic_desc: Soul gems are morpholiths used to bind souls at the moment of death, providing the vital energy required for enchanting, recharging magical items, animating constructs, or fueling destructive spells. Conventional gems shatter upon use, their capacity consumed by the binding. Lore holds that Molag Bal invested a portion of his power in their creation, and black variants are said to be refined in Coldharbour for greater efficiency. Azura's Star is a unique, indestructible relic that functions as a reusable vessel. The value of a filled gem corresponds to the trapped entity's power multiplied by the empty gem's base worth.
topic_desc_basic: Soul gems are specialized morpholiths used to trap the souls of creatures at the moment of death. The captured vital energy is essential for enchanting, recharging magical items, and animating constructs. Standard gems are consumed upon use, though the legendary Azura's Star serves as a reusable vessel.

title: Divine Intervention
topic_desc: Divine Intervention is a Mysticism spell that instantly transports the caster to the nearest Imperial Cult shrine, typically located within an Imperial Legion fort. It serves as both an emergency escape and a rapid transit method across Morrowind, connecting sites such as Buckmoth, Moonmoth, and Ebonheart forts, Fort Pelagiad, Wolverine Hall, and the garrisons at Gnisis and Fort Frostmoth. The spell's alignment with the Imperial Cult reflects the syncretic religious framework established under the Empire, providing faithful and travelers alike with divine safeguard and swift passage to consecrated ground.
topic_desc_basic: Divine Intervention is a Mysticism spell that instantly transports the caster to the nearest Imperial Cult shrine, usually within an Imperial Legion fort. It provides swift travel or escape to consecrated ground at forts across Morrowind, including Ebonheart, Buckmoth, Moonmoth, Pelagiad, Wolverine Hall, and frontier garrisons.

title: Almsivi Intervention
topic_desc: Almsivi Intervention is a mysticism spell of great significance to the Tribunal Temple, invoking the power of the Almsivi to instantly transport the caster to the nearest Tribunal sanctuary. Devotees employ this miracle both as a desperate escape from peril and as a swift conveyance along pilgrimage routes, arriving directly at temple grounds in settlements such as Vivec, Balmora, Ald'ruhn, Gnisis, Molag Mar, and Mournhold. The spell's existence reflects the Temple's doctrine of the Tribunal's guardianship, providing the faithful with a tangible manifestation of divine protection and a practical link to their holy sites across Vvardenfell and beyond.
topic_desc_basic: Almsivi Intervention is a mysticism spell that instantly transports the caster to the nearest Tribunal Temple. Devout followers of the Almsivi use this miracle for swift travel or to escape danger, arriving safely at sanctuaries in major settlements like Vivec, Balmora, Ald'ruhn, Gnisis, Molag Mar, and Mournhold.

title: Mark and Recall
topic_desc: Mark and Recall form a paired system of Mysticism spells enabling instantaneous long-distance transport. The Mark spell anchors a single locational reference point, visible on local maps, while Recall teleports the caster back to that fixed point from any range. Only one Mark can be sustained at a time; recasting it overrides the previous anchor. Without an established Mark, Recall produces no effect. This paired magic is highly valued by mages and travelers for rapid transit and emergency escape, representing a practical application of the school's principles governing spatial manipulation and teleportation.
topic_desc_basic: Mark and Recall are paired Mysticism spells for instantaneous travel. Mark places a single stationary anchor at the caster's location, while Recall teleports the caster back to that anchor from any distance. Only one Mark can exist at a time, and Recall fails without a prior anchor.

title: Propylon Chambers
topic_desc: The Propylon Chambers are ancient teleportation devices housed within the ten Dunmer strongholds of Vvardenfell. Each chamber connects to neighboring strongholds through a network of magical pathways, enabling instantaneous transit across considerable distances. The system requires a Propylon Index—a specialized focusing crystal keyed to a specific destination—to activate transit to that stronghold. Without the appropriate index, the propylon remains inert. The indices are rare and scattered, their locations often unknown or guarded. The network stands as a testament to Dunmer architectural and arcane achievement, though much of its operational knowledge has been lost over the centuries, leaving the chambers largely dormant and their full potential unrealized.
topic_desc_basic: Ancient teleportation chambers built within the Dunmer strongholds of Vvardenfell. The propylon network permits instantaneous travel between strongholds, though each destination requires its corresponding Propylon Index to activate. Most chambers now lie dormant, their indices lost or scattered.

title: Kagrenac's Tools
topic_desc: Kagrenac's Tools are three legendary Dwemer artifacts—Wraithguard, Keening, and Sunder—forged by Lord Kagrenac to tap the divine power of Lorkhan's Heart. Wraithguard is a protective gauntlet, Sunder a hammer to strike the heart and draw power, and Keening a blade to flay and focus that power. Kagrenac's use of these tools during the Battle of Red Mountain coincided with the complete disappearance of the Dwemer. Recovered by Lord Nerevar and Voryn Dagoth, the tools became the center of a fatal dispute. The Tribunal later broke their oath and used them to attain godhood, while Dagoth Ur's unguarded exposure fused him to the Heart. The Dissident Priests consider these artifacts cursed, arguing that their corrupting influence has doomed both the Tribunal and Dagoth Ur.
topic_desc_basic: Kagrenac's Tools are three Dwemer artifacts—Wraithguard, Keening, and Sunder—created to draw upon the divine power of Lorkhan's Heart. Their use at the Battle of Red Mountain coincided with the disappearance of the Dwemer. The Tribunal later used them to attain godhood, though many consider the tools cursed and inherently corrupting.

title: Keening
topic_desc: Keening is a legendary Dwemer short blade forged by Lord Kagrenac, Tonal Architect of the lost Dwemer race. Alongside Sunder and Wraithguard, it forms the essential toolset required to tap the mythic power of the Heart of Lorkhan. Following the Battle of Red Mountain, the Tribunal claimed the tools, though Keening and Sunder were eventually lost during a Third Era pilgrimage to the Heart. The blade now rests within the Odrosal citadel, deep within the Red Mountain region. Keening channels profound tonal resonances; to wield it barehanded is to suffer immediate mortal devastation, necessitating Wraithguard's protective enchantment to safely harness its power.
topic_desc_basic: Keening is a legendary Dwemer dagger forged by Lord Kagrenac. Together with Sunder and Wraithguard, it is one of the three tools required to handle the Heart of Lorkhan. The Tribunal once possessed these artifacts after the Battle of Red Mountain, but Keening was later lost and remains hidden within the Red Mountain region.

title: Sunder
topic_desc: Sunder is a legendary Dwemer hammer crafted by Lord Kagrenac, Tonal Architect of the Dwemer. Alongside Keening and Wraithguard, it forms the toolset necessary to manipulate the Heart of Lorkhan. Following the Battle of Red Mountain, the Almsivi claimed all three tools, though Sunder and Keening were eventually lost during a Third Era pilgrimage to the Heart. The hammer currently resides within Vemynal, held by Dagoth Vemyn of the Sixth House. Without the protective ward of Wraithguard, handling Sunder inflicts a lethal mortal wound upon the wielder.
topic_desc_basic: Sunder is a legendary Dwemer hammer crafted by Lord Kagrenac to manipulate the Heart of Lorkhan. Alongside Keening and Wraithguard, it is essential for tapping the Heart's divine power. Following the Battle of Red Mountain, the Almsivi acquired the tools, but Sunder was later lost and fell into the hands of House Dagoth. It cannot be safely wielded without Wraithguard.

title: Wraithguard
topic_desc: Wraithguard is a legendary Dwemer gauntlet crafted by Lord Kagrenac, the Tonal Architect of the Dwemer. Designed to safely handle the profane tools Keening and Sunder, it is essential for any mortal seeking to tap the mythopoeic energies of the Heart of Lorkhan. Vivec holds the functioning right-hand version, offering it to the Nerevarine for the assault on Red Mountain. Should Vivec perish before bestowing it, the inactive artifact can be recovered and brought to the last living Dwarf, Yagrum Bagarn, who can harmonize it using Kagrenac's journal and planbook; however, activating this jury-rigged version without divine safeguards inflicts severe and permanent harm upon the wielder.
topic_desc_basic: Wraithguard is a legendary Dwemer gauntlet created by Lord Kagrenac. It allows mortals to safely handle Keening and Sunder, the tools required to manipulate the Heart of Lorkhan. Vivec possesses the functioning right-hand gauntlet and grants it to the Nerevarine.

title: Moon-and-Star
topic_desc: Moon-and-Star, formally the great Ring of the Ancestors One-Clan-Under-Moon-and-Star, is a Dwarven ring belonging to the Chimer hero Nerevar. Forged by a smith of the Dwemer Sorcerer-priest Kagrenac and blessed by the Daedric Goddess Azura, it grants its wearer supernatural powers of persuasion. It also serves as indisputable proof of identity, as any unauthorized person who attempts to wear it is killed instantly. Through this artifact, Nerevar united the warring Chimer clans and forged the First Council alongside the Dwemer. In the context of the Nerevarine Prophecies, the ring is the decisive test of identity; only the true reincarnation of Nerevar can wear it and live, providing the authority to again unite the Great Houses and Ashlander clans against Dagoth Ur.
topic_desc_basic: Moon-and-Star is the legendary Dwarven ring of the Chimer hero Nerevar. Blessed by Azura, it grants supernatural powers of persuasion but kills any wearer who is not Nerevar. Ashlander traditions hold that only Nerevar's reincarnation can safely don the ring, making it the ultimate proof of identity in the Nerevarine Prophecies.

title: Azura's Star
topic_desc: Azura's Star is a Daedric artifact created by the Daedric Prince Azura, serving as her prominent symbol. Sometimes called the Twilight Star, it appears as an intricately designed gemstone with eight star-like prongs. In the right hands, it functions as a reusable soul gem of almost unlimited capacity, capturing white souls. Upon use, the trapped soul is freed to journey to Oblivion, emptying the vessel for reuse. This legendary power makes the Star highly sought by mages and assassins. Some believe it can turn living creatures into statues. Mortals once corrupted it to trap black souls, creating the Black Star. Those who wield the artifact are known to Azura's faithful as Star-Bearer.
topic_desc_basic: Azura's Star is a legendary Daedric artifact and symbol of the Daedric Prince Azura. It functions as a reusable soul gem of almost unlimited capacity, making it highly prized by enchanters. The faithful call its wielder the Star-Bearer.

title: Trueflame
topic_desc: Trueflame, the Blade of Nerevar, is a legendary one-handed Dwemer sword from the early First Era. Crafted alongside its twin Hopesfire, the blades represented the pinnacle of Dwemer smithing and bore unearthly fire enchantments. The Dwemer King Dumac presented them as wedding gifts to Lord Indoril Nerevar and Almalexia. Trueflame was shattered during the Battle of Red Mountain circa 1E 700, and its fragments were subsequently lost to history. Tribunal doctrine holds that the weapon possesses the capacity to slay a god, provided it is wielded by one of noble intent. Despite its destruction, the shattered blade remains a potent symbol of Nerevar's legacy and the First Council era.
topic_desc_basic: Trueflame, the Blade of Nerevar, is a legendary Dwemer sword bearing powerful fire enchantments. Given as a wedding gift to Lord Indoril Nerevar and Almalexia by the Dwemer King Dumac, it was shattered during the Battle of Red Mountain circa 1E 700. Its fragments remain lost, though Temple doctrine holds that one of noble intent could use the blade to slay a god.

title: Hopesfire
topic_desc: Hopesfire, also called the Blade of Almalexia, is a one-handed Dwemeri sword from the early First Era. Forged alongside its twin Trueflame, it represents the pinnacle of Dwemer craftsmanship and bears an unearthly fire enchantment. The Dwemer King Dumac presented the blade to Almalexia as a wedding gift upon her union with Lord Indoril Nerevar. While Trueflame belonged to Nerevar, Hopesfire became the iconic weapon of the Goddess of Mercy herself, serving as a symbol of her enduring authority and divine stewardship over Morrowind.
topic_desc_basic: Hopesfire is a legendary Dwemeri blade bearing a powerful fire enchantment. Created in the early First Era alongside its twin, Trueflame, the sword was given to Almalexia as a wedding gift from the Dwemer King Dumac. It remains closely associated with the goddess.

title: Umbra
topic_desc: Umbra is a renowned enchanted longsword of considerable power, currently wielded by a weary Orc warrior who has taken the weapon's name as his own. The blade is infamous for its devastating enchantments, which some attribute to Daedric origins. The Orc, found in the Molag Amur hills near Suran, claims to have grown world-weary after a lifetime of killing. He now seeks a worthy adversary to grant him a warrior's death in combat. Whether the sword's nature contributes to its bearer's existential despair remains a matter of speculation, though such cursed blades are not unknown in Tamrielic lore.
topic_desc_basic: Umbra is a powerful enchanted sword wielded by an Orc warrior of the same name. The weary swordsman dwells in the hills near Suran, seeking a warrior's death in combat. The blade itself is feared for its devastating power in battle.

title: Chrysamere
topic_desc: Chrysamere, the Paladin's Blade, is an ancient adamantium claymore renowned as one of Tamriel's most powerful artifacts. Forged in the late Merethic Era by the Breton swordsmith Asterie Bedel, it synthesizes the craft of man and mer, bearing her maker's mark—a mage's knot—within its heart. Unlike weapons of pure destruction, Chrysamere's enchantments are profoundly defensive, healing its wielder, granting fire resistance, and reflecting hostile spells. The blade does not favor a single champion for long, instead passing between worthy hands. Revered as a holy weapon, it has accumulated many titles, including the Sword of Heroes, the Sword of Kings, and the Blade of Blades.
topic_desc_basic: Chrysamere, the Paladin's Blade, is an ancient adamantium claymore and a revered holy weapon. Forged by the Breton swordsmith Asterie Bedel, it is famed for its powerful defensive enchantments, which heal the wielder, resist fire, and reflect spells rather than merely dealing destruction.

title: The Ebony Mail
topic_desc: The Ebony Mail, also called the Mail of Boethiah, is a legendary Daedric cuirass and sacred relic of the Tribunal Temple. According to Temple doctrine, it rests at the shrine atop Mount Assarnibibi, a site where Molag Bal oversaw the ninety-nine lovers of Boethiah who gave birth to Almalexia. The artifact is deeply intertwined with both Daedric and Tribunal veneration. Only Temple members who have completed the Pilgrimages of the Four Corners and attained Master rank are directed to undertake this final pilgrimage by the Archcanon. Upon activating the mountain's shrine, the Mail is bestowed directly to the pilgrim, a profound honor traditionally culminating in elevation to Patriarch.
topic_desc_basic: The Ebony Mail, or Mail of Boethiah, is a legendary Daedric cuirass venerated as a sacred relic by the Tribunal Temple. It is believed to rest at the shrine atop Mount Assarnibibi, a holy site tied to Boethiah and the birth of Almalexia. The Temple restricts pilgrimage for the Mail to those of high rank who have completed the Four Corners pilgrimages.

title: The Spear of Bitter Mercy
topic_desc: The Spear of Bitter Mercy, also called the Huntsman's Spear or the Spear with Five Points, is a Daedric artifact of enigmatic origin. Though forged by Mehrunes Dagon for the Ritual of the Innocent Quarry, it is now closely associated with Hircine, who wields it as Alrabeg the Hunter. Imbued with maleficent energies that can instantly slay all but the highest Daedra Lords, its use is strictly bound by the rules of the Great Hunt. Sheogorath currently possesses the weapon, though how he acquired it remains unknown. The spear grants its wielder a magical shield and the ability to summon storm atronachs.
topic_desc_basic: The Spear of Bitter Mercy is a legendary Daedric artifact associated with the Great Hunt. Forged by Mehrunes Dagon but most closely linked to Hircine, it possesses lethal enchantments and can summon storm atronachs. Its use is bound by strict rules, and it is currently in Sheogorath's possession.

title: The Daedric Crescent
topic_desc: The Daedric Crescent Blade is a Daedric artifact created by Mehrunes Dagon. During the Imperial Simulacrum, numerous Crescents were wielded by his forces to capture the Battlespire; one, the Sword of the Moon Reiver, was used to banish Dagon from his own realm. When the Empire reclaimed the ruined academy, the Crescents were gathered and destroyed—all but one. Unknown to the Empire, this sole surviving blade remains hidden in Magas Volar, carried by the Dremora Lord Dregas Volar. The weapon slows its target, paralyzes victims, and heavily degrades armor, while occasionally manifesting unexplained green energy.
topic_desc_basic: The Daedric Crescent Blade is a Daedric artifact created by Mehrunes Dagon. Though many such blades were used during the fall of the Battlespire and later destroyed by the Empire, one is rumored to survive, hidden and carried by a Dremora Lord. It inflicts paralysis, slows targets, and heavily degrades armor.

title: The Mazed Band
topic_desc: The Mazed Band is a cursed ring of immense power created by the Clockwork Apostle Barilzar in the mid-Second Era. Designed to teleport multiple individuals across dimensions, its capabilities far exceeded its creator's intent, proving capable of opening rifts in time and space and breaching the gates of Oblivion. To prevent this catastrophic potential, the ring was cursed and stripped of its power so that only a god could safely wield it without being destroyed. This curse presumably killed Barilzar, though he endured as an undead lich, sealed within an abandoned crypt in Old Mournhold alongside his creation. The Tribunal Temple remains aware of the artifact's dangerous existence.
topic_desc_basic: The Mazed Band is a cursed ring of immense power created by the mage Barilzar in the Second Era. Originally designed to teleport groups across dimensions, it could also tear rifts in space and open Oblivion gates. Cursed so only a god can use it safely, the ring is sealed with its undead creator in Old Mournhold.

title: The Mace of Aevar Stone-Singer
topic_desc: The Mace of Aevar Stone-Singer is a revered Skaal artifact forged of stalhrim. Skaal legend holds that the hero Aevar wielded it to amplify the Song of the Earth, restoring the Gift of the Earth and making Solstheim fertile once more. The weapon inflicts severe frost damage upon foes but is extraordinarily heavy. Traditionally, it is bestowed only upon those who complete the Ritual of the Gifts, a sacred pilgrimage across Solstheim. No outsider is known to have received it.
topic_desc_basic: A revered Skaal artifact of stalhrim, the Mace of Aevar Stone-Singer is traditionally awarded to those who complete the Ritual of the Gifts, a sacred Solstheim pilgrimage. Legend says the hero Aevar used it to restore the land's fertility.
